title: Personal Space & Bubble Control
iCan: I can move in my own personal space without touching others.
setup: Open space. Students stand scattered with enough room to extend arms without touching.
warmUp: Freeze & Grow: Move on signal, freeze in a balanced shape when teacher says freeze.
mainActivity: Personal-space bubbles. Students walk, then jog in place while keeping imaginary bubbles from popping (no touching). Add levels: high, medium, low shapes on signal.
challenge: Move to teacher clap patterns or simple music while protecting the bubble. Freeze in a balanced shape on final signal.
coolDown: Sit in personal space. Share one way they kept their bubble safe today.

modifications.easier: Stay seated or kneeling; use arm circles only.
modifications.harder: Add directional changes and speed changes while protecting bubble.
modifications.limitedMobility: Upper-body shapes and seated marches only.
modifications.largeClass: Assign taped spots or visual markers if available; stagger start times.

exitTicket: Teacher visual scan: Can students stop and hold a balanced shape in their own space without touching neighbors?
teacherTip: Use the phrase 'protect your bubble' early — it becomes shared class language for the entire unit and reduces collisions dramatically.
cues: Arms out like a big bubble
Eyes up, look for open space
commonErrors: Students drift into others' space → re-teach 'bubble' with arms extended
Running instead of controlled movement → start with walking only

title: Locomotor Skills – Walk, Jog, Run, Hop
iCan: I can travel using walk, jog, run, and hop while staying in control.
setup: Clear boundaries (cones, lines, or visual cues). Students start on a perimeter or scattered.
warmUp: Follow-the-leader with different locomotor skills called by teacher.
mainActivity: Continuous travel. Teacher calls skill + simple pathway (straight, curved). Practice each skill 30–45 seconds before switching.
challenge: Combine two skills on signal (example: hop then jog). Students create a short two-skill sequence.
coolDown: Slow walk around the boundary + deep breaths. Name the four skills used today.

modifications.easier: Limit to two skills (walk + hop).
modifications.harder: Add levels or force students to change pathway every 10 seconds.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated marches, arm swings, and seated hops (lift hips if able).
modifications.largeClass: Split into two groups; one group moves while other holds shapes, then switch.

exitTicket: On command, students demonstrate one named skill with recognizable form.
teacherTip: Demonstrate the difference between jog (controlled) and run (faster) explicitly — many students treat them as the same.
cues: Hop: take off and land on the same foot
Soft landings — bend ankles, knees, hips
Head up, look where you are going
commonErrors: Hopping on alternating feet (that's skipping) → freeze and re-cue same-foot hop
Looking at feet → remind 'eyes up'

title: Pathways & Direction Changes
iCan: I can travel in straight, curved, and zigzag pathways and change direction on signal.
setup: Open space with clear boundaries. Optional: place 4–6 cones as pathway markers.
warmUp: Shadow movements — teacher demonstrates pathway, students copy.
mainActivity: Pathway Paint: students 'paint' pathways with their bodies. Teacher calls pathway type and direction changes (forward/back, left/right).
challenge: Students design and travel a three-part pathway sequence (example: straight → curved → zigzag).
coolDown: Trace a pathway on the floor with a finger while seated and breathing slowly.

modifications.easier: Only straight and curved pathways.
modifications.harder: Add speed changes and locomotor skill changes inside the pathway.
modifications.limitedMobility: Wheelchair or seated users trace pathways with arms or by rolling.
modifications.largeClass: Use half the space at a time or create two parallel activity zones.

exitTicket: Student demonstrates one pathway type on teacher request.
teacherTip: Have students point the new direction with their whole body before moving — this single cue cuts collisions significantly.
cues: Point your belly button the way you want to go
Curved = smooth arc, not sharp corners
commonErrors: Sharp corners on curved pathways → model smooth arcs
Stopping completely on direction change → practice fluid transitions

title: Levels & Body Shapes in Space
iCan: I can move at high, medium, and low levels and make different body shapes.
setup: Scattered formation with personal space already established.
warmUp: Shape copy-cat: teacher makes a shape, students copy at same level.
mainActivity: Travel while changing levels on signal. Freeze in high/medium/low shapes. Explore wide, narrow, twisted, and round shapes.
challenge: Partner mirror shapes while staying in personal space (no touching).
coolDown: Students choose their favorite shape of the day and share why.

modifications.easier: Only high and low levels.
modifications.harder: Require travel between shape freezes using a specific locomotor skill.
modifications.limitedMobility: Focus on upper-body shapes and seated level changes.
modifications.largeClass: Do partner work in waves or use visual markers for pairs.

exitTicket: On signal, students freeze in a named level (high/medium/low).
teacherTip: Celebrate creative shapes — this builds buy-in for later dance and gymnastics units.
cues: High = as tall as you can
Low = as close to the floor as you can safely
Hold your shape like a statue
commonErrors: Collapsing instead of controlled low level → cue 'strong low shape'
Moving feet during freeze → re-teach stillness

title: Gallop, Slide, Skip Introduction
iCan: I can gallop, slide, and skip with control.
setup: Open space, clear direction of travel (one-way traffic recommended).
warmUp: Quick review of walk, jog, hop.
mainActivity: Isolated practice: gallop (same foot leads) → slide (side orientation) → skip (step-hop). Use visual cues and short practice bouts.
challenge: Travel a pathway using only uneven-beat skills (gallop, slide, skip).
coolDown: Slow-motion skip across the space + reflection on which skill felt easiest.

modifications.easier: Practice only gallop and slide first.
modifications.harder: Combine with pathway and level changes.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated or supported versions focusing on rhythm and arm patterns.
modifications.largeClass: Travel in lanes or waves to avoid collisions.

exitTicket: Student performs one uneven-beat skill with recognizable form.
teacherTip: Many students reverse the lead foot on gallop and slide. Give a clear 'same foot stays in front' cue and check early.
cues: Gallop: same foot stays in front
Slide: belly button faces the side, step-close
Skip: step then hop on the same foot
commonErrors: Alternating lead foot on gallop → freeze and re-set lead foot
Skip turning into a run → slow it down and exaggerate the hop

title: Combining Locomotor Skills + Rhythm
iCan: I can combine locomotor skills and change with a beat or signal.
setup: Open space. Optional simple music with clear beat.
warmUp: Skill review circle — teacher calls skills rapidly.
mainActivity: Continuous travel. Teacher or music cues skill changes. Practice smooth transitions between even-beat and uneven-beat skills.
challenge: Small groups create a 4-skill sequence and perform it for another group.
coolDown: Groups share one sequence and what made transitions smooth.

modifications.easier: Limit to three skills and longer practice time per skill.
modifications.harder: Require specific pathway or level changes inside the sequence.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated rhythm patterns + upper-body locomotor approximations.
modifications.largeClass: Perform sequences in waves or half-class at a time.

exitTicket: Group or individual demonstrates a smooth two-skill transition.
teacherTip: Count out loud during transitions at first ('skip 1-2-3-4, now gallop') so students feel the change point.
cues: Finish one skill cleanly before starting the next
commonErrors: Abrupt stops between skills → practice flowing transitions
Losing the beat → return to teacher-counted cues

title: Safe Travel in General Space – Cooperative Tag
iCan: I can move safely in general space while playing and respecting others' space.
setup: Clear boundaries. Review 'bubble' language from Lesson 1.
warmUp: Bubble review + controlled jogging in general space.
mainActivity: Cooperative tag variations (no elimination). Examples: everyone is 'it' for short bursts, freeze tag with helpers who unfreeze, or locomotor-restricted tag.
challenge: Add a locomotor restriction (only hop or only skip while tagging/fleeing).
coolDown: Circle discussion: What made the space feel safe today? What still needs work?

modifications.easier: Walking tag only.
modifications.harder: Multiple simultaneous taggers + skill restrictions.
modifications.limitedMobility: Include seated or assisted roles (tagger using a soft pool noodle, or designated safe zones).
modifications.largeClass: Play in two smaller zones or use 'zone tag'.

exitTicket: Teacher observation: Are students stopping under control and respecting space?
teacherTip: Ban full-speed running the first two sessions. Build the habit of control first — speed can come later.
cues: Controlled speed — you must be able to stop in two steps
Eyes up, scan for open space
commonErrors: High-speed collisions → immediately reset to walking pace
Students arguing about tags → use clear 'I got tagged' honor system

title: Jumping, Landing & Force Absorption
iCan: I can jump and land softly by bending my hips, knees, and ankles.
setup: Open space. Optional tape lines or poly spots as takeoff/landing markers.
warmUp: Easy hops in place focusing on quiet landings.
mainActivity: Jump for distance and height with emphasis on soft landings. Practice on teacher signals. Progress from two-foot to one-foot takeoffs if ready.
challenge: Create short jump sequences (example: two-foot jump → stick landing → another jump).
coolDown: Gentle leg stretches + self-check: 'Did my landings stay soft today?'

modifications.easier: Small jumps in place only.
modifications.harder: Add 180° turns or combine with locomotor approach.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated or supported 'jumps' focusing on arm drive and controlled return.
modifications.largeClass: Jump in waves or use designated lanes.

exitTicket: Student performs one jump with visible bend in ankles, knees, and hips on landing.
teacherTip: Cue 'quiet feet' — students immediately understand the goal of force absorption.
cues: Bend your ankles, knees, and hips like a shock absorber
Eyes forward, not down at your feet
commonErrors: Stiff-legged landings → exaggerate the bend in demonstration
Looking down → causes loss of balance

title: Partner & Small-Group Space Challenges
iCan: I can move with a partner or small group while sharing space safely.
setup: Students paired or in groups of 3–4. Personal space still respected.
warmUp: Partner mirror — one leads slow movements, other mirrors.
mainActivity: Partner pathways (lead-and-follow), shared shapes, and simple mirroring while traveling.
challenge: Groups of 3–4 design a short movement story using levels and pathways, then perform it.
coolDown: Group reflection: How did you communicate without talking much? What worked?

modifications.easier: Stay with partner mirror only.
modifications.harder: Require specific locomotor skills or timed sequences.
modifications.limitedMobility: Include all students in design and leadership roles; adapt movements as needed.
modifications.largeClass: Assign groups in advance or use numbered teams.

exitTicket: Groups successfully perform a short shared sequence without collisions.
teacherTip: Assign roles (leader, counter, space-checker) so every student has a job and engagement stays high.
commonErrors: One student dominates → rotate leadership every 30–45 seconds
Groups spreading too far → give a maximum area they may use

title: Unit Culmination – Locomotor Showcase + Goal Check
iCan: I can show the locomotor skills and space awareness I have learned and reflect on my progress.
setup: Stations or open space divided into skill zones.
warmUp: Free choice of favorite skills from the unit.
mainActivity: Circuit or stations reviewing key skills. Students rotate and self-assess using simple thumbs-up / side / down.
challenge: Each student creates a short personal routine (3–5 skills) and performs it.
coolDown: Goal reflection: 'What skill am I most proud of? What do I want to improve next?' Teachers capture responses for class goal setting.

modifications.easier: Fewer stations; more guided practice.
modifications.harder: Require students to teach one skill to a partner.
modifications.limitedMobility: All students participate in design and reflection; movements adapted.
modifications.largeClass: Perform routines in small waves.

exitTicket: Student completes a simple self-assessment and names one growth area.
teacherTip: This lesson feeds directly into the AI goal-setting feature. Collect 3–5 common student comments to turn into a class goal.
commonErrors: Students rushing routines → give a clear time limit and practice once first
Vague reflections → provide sentence stems

title: Underhand Toss & Catch to Self
equipment: Minimal (yarn balls, beanbags, or rolled socks)
iCan: I can toss an object underhand to myself and catch it before it bounces twice.
setup: Students scattered in personal space with one soft object each.
warmUp: Body part balance: balance object on different body parts while walking slowly.
mainActivity: Self-toss and catch. Progress from low tosses to higher ones. Cue proper underhand pattern (step with opposite foot, swing arm back to front, release).
challenge: Catch with one hand or alternate hands. Try for consecutive catches.
coolDown: Gentle arm circles + share one tip that helped them catch more consistently.

modifications.easier: Larger, slower objects (scarves or balloons).
modifications.harder: Smaller objects or require clap under the toss before catching.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated tossing; use lighter objects; partner can roll object if needed.
modifications.largeClass: Use whatever soft objects are available; students without objects practice form with imaginary balls.

exitTicket: Student successfully completes 3 consecutive self-tosses and catches.
teacherTip: Start with scarves or plastic bags if real balls are limited — success builds confidence fast.
cues: Swing the arm like a pendulum
Watch the object into your hands
commonErrors: Throwing overhand → freeze and re-model underhand only
Looking away before the catch → cue 'eyes on the ball all the way'

title: Underhand Throw to a Target / Partner
equipment: Minimal (beanbags, yarn balls, hoops or taped targets)
iCan: I can throw underhand to a target or partner with control.
setup: Partners 5–10 feet apart or individual targets on walls/cones.
warmUp: Review self-toss from previous lesson.
mainActivity: Underhand throws to partner (catch and return) or to stationary targets. Focus on accuracy over power.
challenge: Increase distance or reduce target size. Track consecutive successful throws.
coolDown: Partner feedback: one thing your partner did well.

modifications.easier: Shorter distance, larger targets, or rolling instead of throwing.
modifications.harder: Moving targets or non-dominant hand.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated throwing; adjust distance; use ramps if appropriate.
modifications.largeClass: Create multiple short throwing lanes or stations.

exitTicket: Student hits a target or completes a successful partner exchange.
teacherTip: Emphasize 'soft hands' for receivers — many kids tense up and the object bounces out.
cues: Point your belly button at the target
commonErrors: Sidearm or overhand release → re-cue underhand path
Partners standing too close → mark minimum distances

title: Rolling & Trapping a Ball
equipment: Minimal (playground balls or any rolling objects)
iCan: I can roll a ball with control and stop (trap) a rolling ball.
setup: Partners sitting or kneeling facing each other, or individual rolling to a wall.
warmUp: Seated ball rolls around the body.
mainActivity: Partner rolling and trapping. Cue two-handed trap and body behind the ball. Progress to standing rolls.
challenge: Roll through a target gate (two cones) or increase distance.
coolDown: Gentle seated stretches + reflection on control vs power.

modifications.easier: Shorter distance, larger balls.
modifications.harder: One-handed rolls or rolling while moving.
modifications.limitedMobility: All students can participate from seated or supported positions.
modifications.largeClass: Use lines on the floor as rolling lanes.

exitTicket: Successful roll and trap sequence with a partner.
teacherTip: Sitting or kneeling first removes the balance demand so students can focus purely on hand-eye and force control.
cues: Push through the ball, don't slap it
Get your body behind the trap
commonErrors: Slapping the ball → model a smooth push
Ball going sideways → cue 'fingers point where you want it to go'

title: Kicking for Control & Distance
iCan: I can kick a ball with control toward a target or partner.
setup: Open space or kicking lanes. Balls placed in front of students.
warmUp: Toe touches and gentle leg swings.
mainActivity: Stationary ball kicks focusing on plant foot placement and contact with the laces/inside of foot. Progress to short partner kicks and traps.
challenge: Kick for distance or accuracy through gates.
coolDown: Walking collection of balls + calf stretch.

modifications.easier: Larger, lighter balls; shorter distance.
modifications.harder: Moving ball or non-dominant foot.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated kicking with lighter objects or focus on upper-body striking alternatives.
modifications.largeClass: Create multiple short lanes; students retrieve their own ball.

exitTicket: Student demonstrates plant foot beside the ball and controlled contact.
teacherTip: Plant foot position is the #1 error. Spend extra time on 'step next to the ball, not behind it'.
cues: Eyes on the ball at contact
commonErrors: Plant foot too far behind → ball goes up or weak
Toe-poking → cue 'use the inside or laces'

title: Dribbling with Hands (Basketball style)
iCan: I can dribble a ball with my hands while staying in control and looking up.
setup: Personal space or defined dribbling zones.
warmUp: Seated or standing ball taps with fingertips.
mainActivity: Stationary dribble → walking dribble → jogging dribble. Strong emphasis on fingertip control and eyes up.
challenge: Dribble through simple cones or change direction on signal while maintaining dribble.
coolDown: Ball handling tricks (around the waist, legs) at slow speed.

modifications.easier: Larger balls, stationary only, or allow two hands.
modifications.harder: Non-dominant hand, speed changes, or defensive pressure (light).
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated dribbling or table-top bouncing variations.
modifications.largeClass: Assign zones so students are not crossing paths constantly.

exitTicket: Student dribbles 10 consecutive times with eyes up at least part of the time.
teacherTip: Cue 'finger pads, not palms' early and often. Palms cause loss of control.
commonErrors: Slapping with palm → stop and re-teach finger pad push
Watching the ball exclusively → practice 'look at me while dribbling'

title: Dribbling with Feet (Soccer style)
iCan: I can dribble a ball with my feet using small touches while keeping my head up.
setup: Open space with clear boundaries. One ball per student if possible.
warmUp: Toe taps on top of the ball and gentle pulls back and forth.
mainActivity: Stationary foot taps → walking dribble with inside of both feet → controlled direction changes.
challenge: Dribble through a short course or keep the ball close while changing speed.
coolDown: Ball between feet, gentle side-to-side rolls + reflection.

modifications.easier: Larger balls, slower pace, or allow more space between students.
modifications.harder: Weaving through cones or weak-foot only.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated or assisted versions; focus on accuracy of contact.
modifications.largeClass: Use lanes or half the class active at a time.

exitTicket: Student keeps the ball within 2–3 feet while moving 10+ steps.
teacherTip: Small touches are everything. Students want to kick hard — constantly cue 'soft touches, ball stays close'.
cues: Soft touches with the inside of the foot
Ball stays close to your feet
commonErrors: Kicking the ball too far ahead → stop and practice tiny touches
Using only one foot → require alternating feet

title: Striking with Hands (Volley / Overhead)
equipment: Minimal (beach balls, balloons, or light playground balls)
iCan: I can strike a ball upward with my hands and keep it in the air or send it to a partner.
setup: Personal space or partner pairs. Light objects preferred for success.
warmUp: Balloon or scarf tapping with different body parts.
mainActivity: Self-volleys (keep-ups) with finger pads or open hands. Progress to partner underhand volleys.
challenge: Consecutive keep-ups or partner rallies of 5+ exchanges.
coolDown: Gentle shoulder stretches + share a control tip.

modifications.easier: Balloons or very light balls; allow catch between strikes.
modifications.harder: Smaller balls or non-dominant hand.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated striking; lower targets; partner assists with tosses.
modifications.largeClass: Use whatever light objects exist; focus on form over equipment equality.

exitTicket: Student keeps an object in the air for 3+ consecutive strikes or completes a short partner rally.
teacherTip: Balloons are magic for this skill — almost every student experiences success quickly.
cues: Contact with finger pads or flat hands
Bend knees and get under the ball
commonErrors: Swinging with closed fists → open the hands
Contacting the ball too late → cue 'get under it early'

title: Striking with Implements (Short-handled)
equipment: Minimal to Full (paddles, rackets, or open hands if none available)
iCan: I can strike a ball or object with a short-handled implement using proper grip and orientation.
setup: Stations or open space. Safety spacing critical.
warmUp: Shadow swings without a ball, focusing on side orientation and grip.
mainActivity: Strike a suspended ball, ball off a tee/cone, or tossed ball. Emphasize side to target and level swing path.
challenge: Hit for distance or accuracy to a target zone.
coolDown: Equipment collection + forearm stretch.

modifications.easier: Larger striking surfaces, stationary ball, or hand striking only.
modifications.harder: Smaller objects or moving tosses.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated striking; shorter implements; partner tosses.
modifications.largeClass: Rotate small groups through striking stations; others work on previous skills.

exitTicket: Student demonstrates side orientation and makes solid contact.
teacherTip: If you have no paddles, students can use open hands or even a rolled newspaper — the body position cues are the same.
cues: Watch the ball all the way to contact
commonErrors: Facing the target square instead of side-on → re-position feet
Swinging too hard and losing balance → cue 'smooth and controlled'

title: Combining Manipulative Skills – Stations
equipment: Minimal (variety of balls and soft objects)
iCan: I can apply different manipulative skills in a station format and work independently or with a partner.
setup: 4–6 stations around the space, each focused on a previously taught skill.
warmUp: Quick review of key cues for the skills in rotation.
mainActivity: Students rotate through stations (throwing, kicking, dribbling, striking, etc.). Short time at each (3–5 min).
challenge: At one station, set a personal record (consecutive catches, dribbles, etc.).
coolDown: Group share of favorite station and one skill that improved.

modifications.easier: Fewer stations, longer time, more teacher guidance.
modifications.harder: Add performance challenges or peer coaching roles.
modifications.limitedMobility: Every station has an accessible version; students choose appropriate challenge.
modifications.largeClass: Duplicate popular stations or run two parallel circuits.

exitTicket: Student participates fully at 3+ stations and can name one cue they used.
teacherTip: Post simple visual cues at each station so students can self-correct without waiting for you.
cues: Use the cues you already know
commonErrors: Students lingering at favorite stations → use a clear rotation signal
Off-task behavior → shorter intervals and active supervision

title: Unit Culmination – Manipulative Skills Showcase
iCan: I can demonstrate the manipulative skills I have learned and reflect on my progress.
setup: Open space or stations for choice.
warmUp: Free practice of any manipulative skill from the unit.
mainActivity: Choice circuit or partner challenges reviewing key skills. Students self-assess using simple criteria.
challenge: Create a short skill combination (example: dribble → stop → underhand throw to partner).
coolDown: Reflection and goal conversation: Which skill improved the most? What do you want to keep practicing?

modifications.easier: More guided choices and partner support.
modifications.harder: Students design and teach a mini-station to peers.
modifications.limitedMobility: Full inclusion in design, demonstration (adapted), and reflection.
modifications.largeClass: Perform in waves; use peer observers.

exitTicket: Student completes a self-assessment and identifies one strength and one growth area.
teacherTip: Capture student reflections — they become excellent material for the next class goal with the AI assistant.
cues: Show clean form, not just power
commonErrors: Focusing only on the 'fun' skills → gently require at least one less-preferred skill
Vague goal statements → provide stems ('I want to get better at ___ by ___')

title: Heart Rate Awareness – Finding Your Pulse
iCan: I can find my pulse and notice how activity changes my heart rate.
setup: Open space. Students can sit or stand.
warmUp: Easy marching in place while breathing normally.
mainActivity: Teach two pulse points (wrist and neck). Practice finding pulse at rest (count for 15 sec × 4). Then do 1 minute of jumping jacks or high knees and recount. Compare numbers.
challenge: Students predict which activity will raise heart rate more, then test two different activities.
coolDown: Slow breathing + discuss why heart rate goes up during activity.

modifications.easier: Teacher counts with students; use only wrist pulse.
modifications.harder: Graph rest vs active heart rate; try recovery time after activity.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated marches, arm circles, or any safe elevated activity.
modifications.largeClass: Demonstrate on a volunteer first; students work in pairs to help each other find pulse.

exitTicket: Student can point to a pulse location and say whether their heart was faster or slower after activity.
teacherTip: Many kids press too hard on the neck — cue 'gentle touch, like feeling a butterfly'.
commonErrors: Pressing too hard → pulse disappears
Counting for random times → always use same 15-second window

title: Muscular Strength – Bodyweight Basics
iCan: I can perform basic strength movements with good form.
setup: Personal space for each student.
warmUp: Arm circles, gentle squats, march in place.
mainActivity: Teach and practice: wall or knee push-ups, bodyweight squats, glute bridges, and plank (or modified plank). Short sets with rest. Focus on form over quantity.
challenge: Create a 4-move strength circuit and complete 2 rounds.
coolDown: Gentle stretches for chest, legs, and shoulders.

modifications.easier: Wall push-ups, sit-to-stand from chair, shorter holds.
modifications.harder: Full push-ups, single-leg bridges, longer planks.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated strength options (arm presses, seated marches, band-free rows with towel).
modifications.largeClass: All students move together on teacher count; no equipment needed.

exitTicket: Student demonstrates one strength movement with recognizable form.
teacherTip: Quality over quantity — stop sets before form breaks down.
commonErrors: Sagging hips in plank → cue 'squeeze your belly'
Rushing reps → slow the tempo

title: Flexibility & Cool-Down Habits
iCan: I can hold stretches safely and understand why we cool down.
setup: Students seated or standing in personal space.
warmUp: Easy locomotor movement for 2 minutes.
mainActivity: Teach 5–6 major stretches (hamstrings, quads, calves, shoulders, chest, gentle twist). Hold 15–20 seconds each. Emphasize no bouncing.
challenge: Students lead one stretch for the class.
coolDown: Discussion: When should we stretch? How does it feel?

modifications.easier: Shorter holds; seated versions only.
modifications.harder: Add dynamic mobility movements before static stretches.
modifications.limitedMobility: All stretches have seated or supported versions.
modifications.largeClass: Teacher models; students mirror.

exitTicket: Student names one muscle they stretched and holds a stretch with control.
teacherTip: Never force a stretch — 'mild pull is ok, pain is not'.
commonErrors: Bouncing → re-cue stillness
Holding breath → remind to breathe

title: Personal Fitness Challenge Day
iCan: I can set a small fitness goal and work toward it with effort.
setup: Stations or open space for choice activities.
warmUp: Student choice of easy movement.
mainActivity: Students choose 2–3 fitness challenges (e.g., how many controlled squats, how long a plank, how many jump ropes if available, heart-rate recovery). Record a baseline. Practice with effort.
challenge: Set a realistic target for next time and write it down.
coolDown: Share one goal with a partner; stretch.

modifications.easier: Fewer challenges; teacher helps set goals.
modifications.harder: Include recovery heart rate or multi-skill challenges.
modifications.limitedMobility: Fully inclusive challenge options for every student.
modifications.largeClass: Use a simple recording sheet or partner recording.

exitTicket: Student has a written or verbal personal fitness goal.
teacherTip: Celebrate effort and improvement, not only the highest numbers.
commonErrors: Goals too big → help scale them down
Comparing only to peers → refocus on personal progress

title: Cooperative Challenges – No Elimination
iCan: I can work with others to solve a movement challenge without anyone being out.
setup: Open space. Clear boundaries.
warmUp: Partner mirror movements.
mainActivity: Play cooperative games only: group balance challenges, 'everyone across the river' style problems, collective freeze games where the group succeeds together.
challenge: Groups invent one new cooperative rule and try it.
coolDown: Discuss what helped the group succeed.

modifications.easier: Smaller groups; simpler challenges.
modifications.harder: Add time limits or silent communication only.
modifications.limitedMobility: Every challenge has roles that include all abilities.
modifications.largeClass: Multiple small groups working in parallel.

exitTicket: Student can name one way they helped the group.
teacherTip: Ban elimination language early — 'we're solving this together' becomes the norm.
commonErrors: Students creating their own elimination rules → reset expectations
One leader dominating → rotate leadership

title: Strategy Games – Offense & Defense Concepts
iCan: I can use simple offensive and defensive ideas in a small-sided game.
setup: Small-sided playing areas. Soft balls or beanbags if available.
warmUp: Tag variations that practice chasing and fleeing.
mainActivity: Introduce concepts: create space, protect space, pass to open player, defend the path to the goal. Play modified small-sided games with frequent pauses for strategy talk.
challenge: Teams set one strategy focus for a short game segment.
coolDown: Team debrief: What strategy worked?

modifications.easier: Fewer players per side; walking pace only.
modifications.harder: Add conditions (must pass 2 times before scoring).
modifications.limitedMobility: Include zone or support roles that matter to the team.
modifications.largeClass: Multiple small games instead of one large game.

exitTicket: Student can explain one offensive or defensive idea they used.
teacherTip: Freeze the game often for 20-second strategy huddles — learning sticks better than continuous play.
commonErrors: Everyone crowds the ball → cue spacing
No passing → require a pass before a score attempt

title: Trust & Communication Movement Tasks
iCan: I can give clear directions and listen carefully so my partner or group succeeds.
setup: Pairs or small groups. Clear safe space.
warmUp: Partner lead-and-follow (leader moves, partner mirrors).
mainActivity: Blindfolded (or eyes-closed) partner walks with verbal guidance only; group shape challenges where only one person can see a target shape; silent communication tasks.
challenge: Groups complete a course using only agreed hand signals.
coolDown: Reflect on what made communication clear or confusing.

modifications.easier: Eyes open; simpler pathways.
modifications.harder: Full silence except one designated speaker.
modifications.limitedMobility: Roles adapted so every student can lead and support.
modifications.largeClass: Pairs first, then small groups.

exitTicket: Student can describe one clear communication habit that helped.
teacherTip: Safety first with eyes-closed activities — small spaces, slow speed, and clear stop signals.
commonErrors: Too many people talking → assign one speaker
Moving too fast → mandatory slow pace

title: Beat Awareness & Movement to Music
iCan: I can move in time with a steady beat.
setup: Open space. Music with clear beat if available; otherwise teacher claps/counts.
warmUp: Clap and march to a steady beat.
mainActivity: Move locomotor skills on the beat. Freeze on rest. Explore different body parts keeping the beat. Simple mirror dances.
challenge: Create a 4-beat movement pattern and repeat it.
coolDown: Slow swaying movements + soft breathing.

modifications.easier: Slower tempo; seated beat movements.
modifications.harder: Faster tempo; combine locomotor + non-locomotor on beat.
modifications.limitedMobility: Upper-body and seated rhythmic patterns fully included.
modifications.largeClass: Everyone faces the same direction; teacher leads.

exitTicket: Student moves or claps on beat for a short phrase.
teacherTip: If you have no music, a simple drum, desk, or even two sticks works perfectly.
commonErrors: Moving between beats → slow down and exaggerate
Only arms moving → add feet or whole body

title: Simple Dance Sequences
iCan: I can learn and perform a short dance sequence.
setup: Students in rows or circle so everyone can see.
warmUp: Isolations (head, shoulders, hips) to easy music or counts.
mainActivity: Teach a short 4- or 8-count sequence step by step. Practice in parts, then whole. Add expression and levels.
challenge: Pairs or groups add one original 4-count and perform the full sequence.
coolDown: Free dance at low intensity + share favorite move.

modifications.easier: Fewer counts; repeat the same step.
modifications.harder: Faster music; directional changes; partner work.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated or adapted choreography that keeps the same timing and expression.
modifications.largeClass: Teach facing the same way; use clear visual cues.

exitTicket: Student performs most of the sequence with the group.
teacherTip: Teach one 4-count at a time and only add the next when most students have the first.
commonErrors: Rushing ahead of the count → return to slow practice
Looking only at feet → cue eyes up

title: Creative Movement & Expression
iCan: I can create movements that show an idea, feeling, or story.
setup: Open space with room to move freely.
warmUp: Move like different animals or weather on teacher prompts.
mainActivity: Prompts: move like you are happy / strong / sneaky / heavy / light. Then small groups create a short movement story with a beginning, middle, and end.
challenge: Groups perform their story; audience guesses the idea.
coolDown: Slow reflective movement + one word about how it felt.

modifications.easier: Individual prompts only; no performance.
modifications.harder: Longer stories; require specific levels and pathways.
modifications.limitedMobility: Expression is the focus — any body part can carry the idea.
modifications.largeClass: Perform in waves of small groups.

exitTicket: Student contributes at least one clear expressive movement.
teacherTip: There is no wrong creative movement — praise commitment and clarity of idea.
cues: Show it with your whole body
commonErrors: Self-consciousness → start with eyes-closed exploration
Copying only → require one original idea per student

title: Static Balance & Bases of Support
iCan: I can balance in different shapes using wide and narrow bases of support.
setup: Personal space. Optional lines or spots on floor.
warmUp: Freeze in balanced shapes on signal.
mainActivity: Explore balances on 1–4 body parts. Compare wide vs narrow bases. Hold balances for increasing time. Partner matching balances.
challenge: Create a sequence of three balances with smooth transitions.
coolDown: Gentle yoga-style holds + breathing.

modifications.easier: Two-foot balances only; hold near a wall.
modifications.harder: Eyes closed; unstable surfaces if safe mats available.
modifications.limitedMobility: Seated or supported balances focusing on control and shape.
modifications.largeClass: All students balance at once; teacher scans for safety.

exitTicket: Student holds a controlled balance on a reduced base for 5+ seconds.
teacherTip: Cue 'eyes on a fixed point' — it dramatically improves balance.
commonErrors: Looking around → fix gaze
Holding breath → remind to breathe

title: Landing Safely & Rolling
iCan: I can land softly and perform a basic roll with control.
setup: Clear space. Mats if you have them; otherwise carpet or grass.
warmUp: Jump and land quietly in place.
mainActivity: Review soft landings (ankles-knees-hips). Progress to log rolls and, if ready, basic forward roll progressions with strong safety emphasis. Never force rolling.
challenge: Jump → soft land → controlled roll sequence.
coolDown: Stretch and discuss when soft landings matter in real life.

modifications.easier: Landings only; rocking on back instead of full rolls.
modifications.harder: Varied jump directions into landings; smoother roll connections.
modifications.limitedMobility: Focus on controlled lowering and upper-body rolling patterns as appropriate.
modifications.largeClass: Small groups rotate; strong spotting culture if rolling.

exitTicket: Student demonstrates a soft landing with visible bend in ankles, knees, and hips.
teacherTip: If you are not confident teaching forward rolls, stay with landings and log rolls — still excellent content.
commonErrors: Stiff landings → exaggerate the bend
Rolling with straight legs/back → stop and regress

title: Weight Transfer & Simple Inversions Intro
iCan: I can transfer weight from feet to hands safely and with control.
setup: Personal space; mats if available.
warmUp: Animal walks (bear, crab, frog) to load arms gently.
mainActivity: Practice weight on hands: donkey kicks (small), feet higher than hands on a low surface if available, or simply strong plank to downward-dog style transfers. Emphasize shoulder strength and control over height.
challenge: Smooth sequence: plank → weight shift → return to feet.
coolDown: Wrist and shoulder stretches; discuss safety.

modifications.easier: Remain in plank and short weight shifts only.
modifications.harder: Controlled kick-ups with spotter culture; cartwheel progressions if previously taught.
modifications.limitedMobility: Upper-body loading alternatives that are appropriate for the student.
modifications.largeClass: Strict spacing; no freestyle inverted attempts.

exitTicket: Student shows controlled weight on hands and safe return to feet.
teacherTip: Prioritize shoulder stability and landing safety over any inverted skill.
commonErrors: Dumping weight onto head → immediate stop
Bending arms → cue locked soft elbows

title: Outdoor Awareness & Hiking Skills (Schoolyard)
iCan: I can move safely outdoors and use basic trail/pace awareness.
setup: Schoolyard, field, or safe outdoor route.
warmUp: Dynamic walking and light jogging.
mainActivity: Practice pace control, line-of-sight with a partner, simple orienteering with landmarks, and leave-no-trace ideas. Walk/hike a route with purpose.
challenge: Groups navigate a short landmark course and return on time.
coolDown: Stretch outdoors; notice heart rate and breathing.

modifications.easier: Shorter route; more frequent stops.
modifications.harder: Add pacing goals or map-simple challenges.
modifications.limitedMobility: Fully accessible routes and roles (navigator, timer, observer).
modifications.largeClass: Multiple loops or staggered start times.

exitTicket: Student can explain one outdoor safety or pacing habit.
teacherTip: Even a blacktop loop can teach pacing, awareness, and outdoor habits.
cues: Stay where you can see your partner
Leave the space better than you found it
commonErrors: Racing ahead → mandatory partner check-ins
Ignoring boundaries → clear visual markers

title: Lifetime Activity Exploration
iCan: I can try different lifetime activities and notice which ones I enjoy.
setup: Stations representing different lifetime activities (walking, strength, dance, skill games, mindfulness movement).
warmUp: Easy full-body movement.
mainActivity: Rotate through 4–5 lifetime activity stations. At each, students rate enjoyment and effort honestly.
challenge: Choose one activity to revisit and set a tiny personal goal for it.
coolDown: Share which activity felt best and why.

modifications.easier: Fewer stations; longer time at each.
modifications.harder: Students design one station for peers.
modifications.limitedMobility: Every station has an accessible version.
modifications.largeClass: Duplicate popular stations.

exitTicket: Student names one lifetime activity they would like to keep doing.
teacherTip: This lesson plants seeds for adult activity habits — treat preferences seriously.
commonErrors: Only choosing friends' stations → require full rotation first
Dismissing new activities quickly → minimum time rule

title: Community & Home Activity Planning
iCan: I can make a simple plan to be active outside of PE class.
setup: Classroom or gathering space; paper optional.
warmUp: Brainstorm active things kids can do at home or in the neighborhood.
mainActivity: Students create a realistic 1-week mini activity plan (3–5 short sessions). Include what, when, and with whom if relevant.
challenge: Identify one barrier and one solution (weather, space, motivation).
coolDown: Optional share-out of plans; encouragement circle.

modifications.easier: Plan for only 2 days; teacher provides templates.
modifications.harder: Include variety (strength + aerobic + outdoor).
modifications.limitedMobility: Plans built around each student's real options.
modifications.largeClass: Pair-share instead of whole-class sharing.

exitTicket: Student has a concrete activity plan for at least two days.
teacherTip: Keep plans tiny and doable — success builds the habit.
commonErrors: Overly ambitious plans → help scale down
No schedule → add a day/time

title: Skills Showcase Stations
iCan: I can demonstrate skills from the year and notice my growth.
setup: 6–8 stations covering locomotor, manipulative, fitness, balance, and cooperative skills.
warmUp: Free choice practice at any station.
mainActivity: Rotate through stations. At each, students perform and give themselves a simple self-score (1–3) on form and effort.
challenge: Pick one skill that improved the most this year and show it to a partner.
coolDown: Whole-class reflection on growth.

modifications.easier: Fewer stations; more teacher support.
modifications.harder: Peer coaching roles at stations.
modifications.limitedMobility: All stations accessible; growth is the focus.
modifications.largeClass: Duplicate stations; staggered rotations.

exitTicket: Student identifies one skill that improved and one still growing.
teacherTip: Take photos or notes if appropriate — powerful for parent communication and student pride.
commonErrors: Rushing stations → longer time per station
Only comparing to others → refocus on personal progress

title: Class Goals Celebration & Reflection
iCan: I can reflect on our class goals and set a new personal movement goal.
setup: Circle or comfortable gathering space.
warmUp: Favorite movement from the year — student choice.
mainActivity: Review class goals set earlier. Celebrate progress (even partial). Students write or share a new personal movement goal for summer or next term.
challenge: Offer one specific encouragement to a classmate.
coolDown: Group appreciation and a final active game of the class's choice.

modifications.easier: Verbal goals only; teacher records.
modifications.harder: Goals include a simple measurement plan.
modifications.limitedMobility: Full participation in reflection and celebration.
modifications.largeClass: Pair and small-group sharing.

exitTicket: Student has a forward-looking personal movement goal.
teacherTip: End the year on identity: 'We are people who move and improve.'
commonErrors: Vague goals → provide stems
Focusing only on what was missed → highlight gains first

title: Favorite Games Tournament (Inclusive)
iCan: I can play favorite games with fair play and inclusion.
setup: Spaces for 2–3 favorite class games rotated during the period.
warmUp: Student-led warm-up from a previous unit.
mainActivity: Play the class's highest-rated games with clear fair-play expectations and no elimination. Rotate so everyone plays multiple games.
challenge: Students help referee or modify a rule to make a game more inclusive.
coolDown: Thank-you circle and final stretch.

modifications.easier: One game only; more scaffolding.
modifications.harder: Student captains manage rotations and fairness.
modifications.limitedMobility: Rule adaptations agreed before play starts.
modifications.largeClass: Multiple concurrent games with clear zones.

exitTicket: Student demonstrates fair play and can name one inclusive adjustment used.
teacherTip: Let students vote on games in advance so the final day feels owned by the class.
commonErrors: Old elimination habits return → pause and reset
Arguments → use a quick student mediation routine
